item.title: Sphere decomposition for finite subgroups of 3-manifold mapping class groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.31798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a closed, oriented 3-manifold $M$, we show that any finite subgroup of its mapping class group preserves an isotopy class of filling sphere system on $M$. This is an isotopy version of the "equivariant sphere theorem" of Meeks-Yau. As part of our analysis, we establish a bijection between simplices of the Guirardel--Levitt outer space for $\pi_1(M)$ and filling sphere systems in $M$, generalizing an argument of Hatcher. We also compute the image of $\mathrm{Homeo}(M)\to\mathrm{Out}(\pi_1M)$ for any such $M$.
item.dc:creator: Corey Bregman, Bena Tshishiku

item.title: The $d$-invariant of surgeries on $2$-component L-space links
item.description: arXiv:2610.31853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gorsky, B. Liu and Moore provided a formula for the $d$-invariants of integral surgeries on $2$-component $L$-space links with linking number $0$. This paper generalizes these results to the nonzero linking number case. We describe how the $d$-invariant depends on the definiteness of the framing matrix and provide formulae for certain families of positive definite framings, as well as a skein relation for non-algebraically split links.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Li

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^\mu, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Conway polynomials of $Th(p,q)$ and $Th(q,p)$: a proof of Takemura's conjecture
item.description:
arXiv:2610.32269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Takemura conjectured that the Conway polynomials $\sum a_\ell z^\ell$ of the Turk's head link $Th(p,q)$ and $\sum b_\ell z^\ell$ of $Th(q,p)$ satisfy $a_\ell=b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv0,1\pmod 4$ and $a_\ell=-b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv2,3\pmod4$, and proved it for $q=2,3$. We prove it for all $p,q\ge1$, knots and links. Equivalently, $
abla_{Th(q,p)}(z)=c\,
abla_{Th(p,q)}(iz)$ with $c=1$ if $\gcd(p,q)$ is odd and $c=-i$ if it is even. The proof combines a product formula $
abla_{Th(p,q)}(z)^2=\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\prod_{k=1}^{q-1}(z^2+2\cos rac{2\pi k}{q}-2\cos rac{2\pi j}{p})$, which comes from the reduced Burau representation, with the leading coefficients, read off the Seifert surface of the closed braid.
item.dc:creator: Werner Alois Stanggassinger

item.title: Angle cocycles, Euler characteristic, and simplicial volume of smooth manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.32342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A celebrated conjecture of Gromov states that for closed aspherical manifolds, the vanishing of simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic. We prove Gromov's conjecture for closed convex projective manifolds and, more generally, for closed orientable smooth manifolds admitting an immersed straightening. Generalising the straightening of simplices in properly convex domains in real projective space, we introduce the notion of immersed straightening and prove that, for every integer $d\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that every closed orientable smooth $d$-manifold $M$ admitting an immersed straightening satisfies $|\chi(M)|\le C_d||M||$.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Bucher, Stefano Francaviglia, Grazia Rago

item.title: Exact bounded cohomology of measure-preserving homeomorphism groups of nonorientable hyperbolic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.32475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a closed, connected, non-orientable hyperbolic manifold, and let $\mu$ be a good measure on $M$. Denote by $Homeo_0(M,\mu)$ the identity component of the group of $\mu$-preserving homeomorphisms. For every $d\geq2$, we prove that $\dim\overline{EH}_b^d\bigl(Homeo_0(M,\mu)\bigr)=\infty$, where $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denotes reduced exact bounded cohomology in degree $d$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Brandenbursky

item.title: Simple homotopy types of smooth four-manifolds with finite fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2610.32706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct closed smooth $4$-manifolds with finite fundamental group which are homotopy equivalent but not simple homotopy equivalent, even after taking a connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$. Our explicit examples have remarkably large fundamental groups; in particular, the smallest examples we obtain have fundamental groups of order roughly $10^{10^{42}}$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Kasprowski, John Nicholson

item.title: Counting curves with bounded intersection
item.description: arXiv:2610.32723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper counts curves, and multicurves, on hyperbolic surfaces, providing explicit upper bounds that depend polynomially on length and exponentially in terms of an upper bound on self-intersection.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Parlier

item.title: Veering triangulations of once-punctured torus bundles are unique
item.description: arXiv:2610.32771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that each hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundle has exactly one veering triangulation. We also find manifolds for which the exact number of veering structures is known and is greater than one. Finally, we give new examples of manifolds without veering triangulations.
item.dc:creator: Saul Schleimer, Henry Segerman

item.title: The space of equators has infinite Hofer's diameter
item.description: arXiv:2610.31940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We settle several questions about Hofer's geometry of the two-sphere. We prove that the space of equators has infinite Hofer diameter, construct simple commutators of arbitrarily large Hofer norm, and exhibit a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism whose iterates escape to infinity in Hofer distance from the set of autonomous diffeomorphisms. Finally, we construct a bi-Lipschitz group monomorphism from the free group of rank two, equipped with its conjugation-invariant generator norm, into the Hamiltonian group equipped with Hofer's metric. The proof rests on an interplay between Lagrangian Floer theory in the fourth symmetric product of the sphere and combinatorial group theory. This paper was written with substantial assistance from AI.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Polterovich, Egor Shelukhin

item.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
item.description: arXiv:2610.32320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Miura

item.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.16600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and \c{S}avk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.
item.dc:creator: Werner Alois Stanggassinger

item.title: Weinstein Handlebodies for the Painlev\'e Betti Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.17352v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the generic fibre of the Betti moduli space associated to any of the ten Painlev\'e equations coincides with the result of attaching Weinstein handles along the Stokes Legendrian, and provide Weinstein handlebody diagrams for each of them in the process. We moreover extend the procedure for obtaining presentations in Gompf normal form of Weinstein manifolds obtained by attaching handles to Legendrian lifts of cooriented curves in surfaces to their unit cotangent bundle to the case where the surface may have nonempty boundary.
item.dc:creator: Jo\"el D. Beimler, William E. Olsen

item.title: A Topological Figiel-Lindenstrauss-Milman Theorem and its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2609.10402v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a topological generalization of the Figiel--Lindenstrauss--Milman inequality, answering a recent question of Frick, Hosseini, and Vasileuski: every nonempty strongly regular CW complex with $v$ vertices, $f$ maximal cells, and a free involution that permutes its cells has $\mathbb Z/2$-index at most $4\log v\log f$. The classical inequality for centrally symmetric polytopes is the special case of polytope boundaries. As an application, we show that every finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb RP^d$ has at least $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt d))$ vertices. The previous best lower bound was $\Omega(d^2)$. We also construct triangulations with $\exp(O(\sqrt d))$ vertices. Using the same method, we prove a low-dimensional Postnikov factorization theorem, which gives similar vertex lower bounds for several classical families, such as complex and quaternionic projective spaces, the $d$-torus, closed symplectic and aspherical manifolds, Grassmannians, classical Lie groups, and spherical space forms. Further applications include results in learning theory, convex geometry, computational topology, and topological bounds for chromatic numbers and Vietoris--Rips complexes.
item.dc:creator: Florian Frick, Kaave Hosseini, Eric Myzelev, Arya Narnapatti, Aliaksei Vasileuski

item.title: Spherical and affine Artin groups, finite quotients, and the isomorphism problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.27171v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the smallest non-abelian quotients of spherical and affine Artin groups. Usually, these are isomorphic to the smallest non-abelian quotients of the corresponding Coxeter groups. As applications, we deduce that two affine Artin groups are isomorphic if and only if their Coxeter diagrams are isomorphic and that irreducible spherical Artin groups are distinguished from each other by their finite quotient groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Thomas Ng, Kaitlin Ragosta, Nancy Scherich, Yvon Verberne

item.title: Cluster structures from Legendrian double twist knots: a comparative approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.02086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We undertake a systematic comparison of cluster algebras associated to Legendrian knots of the same smooth knot type. We describe a cluster structure on the m-graded augmentation variety of Legendrian representatives of a family of double twist knots that includes all orientably Lagrangian fillable twist knots. For different Legendrian representatives of the same smooth knot type, we show that these cluster structures are equivalent. Along the way, we characterize the representatives that admit Maslov-m exact Lagrangian fillings, construct a Catalan number of such fillings for each representative, and show that any Maslov-0 fillable representative is Legendrian isotopic to the (-1)-framed closure of a positive braid. Finally, we give two Legendrian representatives of a cabled twist knot that yield equivalent cluster structures of infinite type.
item.dc:creator: James Hughes, Jiajie Ma
